Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Conservative Party Manifesto 2015: Summary

## Economic Plan
The manifesto centers on continuing the party's "long-term economic plan." The Conservatives claim to have transformed Britain from economic crisis to the fastest-growing major advanced economy. Key economic pledges include:

- Eliminating the deficit and running a surplus by 2018-19
- Raising the tax-free Personal Allowance to £12,500
- Increasing the 40p Income Tax threshold to £50,000
- No increases to VAT, National Insurance, or Income Tax
- Cracking down on tax evasion and aggressive avoidance
- Building a "Northern Powerhouse" with £13 billion transport investment

## Jobs and Business
The party commits to creating 2 million new jobs and achieving "full employment." Business-focused policies include:

- Delivering 3 million new apprenticeships
- Abolishing employers' National Insurance for under-21s
- Cutting red tape by £10 billion
- Maintaining competitive business tax rates
- Supporting small businesses through rate reviews and prompt payment initiatives

## Welfare Reform
The manifesto promises a "fairer" welfare system:

- Reducing the household benefit cap from £26,000 to £23,000
- Rolling out Universal Credit
- Freezing working-age benefits for two years
- Replacing Jobseeker's Allowance for 18-21 year-olds with time-limited Youth Allowance
- Removing automatic Housing Benefit entitlement for young jobseekers

## Immigration
Pledging "controlled immigration," key proposals include:

- Maintaining the ambition for net migration in "tens of thousands"
- Requiring EU migrants to work four years before claiming tax credits or child benefit
- Introducing residency requirements for social housing
- Ending benefits for EU jobseekers

## NHS and Health
Healthcare commitments include:

- Increasing NHS spending by at least £8 billion above inflation by 2020
- Delivering a "truly 7-day NHS"
- Guaranteeing same-day GP appointments for over-75s
- Integrating health and social care
- Continuing dementia research funding

## Education
Education reforms focus on:

- Ensuring good school places for all children
- Converting failing and "coasting" schools into academies
- Opening 500+ new free schools
- Protecting school funding
- Removing caps on university places

## Housing
Housing policies include:

- Building 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% below market price for first-time buyers under 40
- Extending Help to Buy and introducing Help to Buy ISAs
- Extending Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants
- Protecting the Green Belt

## Europe
The landmark EU commitment:

- Holding an in-out referendum on EU membership by end of 2017
- Negotiating a new settlement with the EU
- Scrapping the Human Rights Act and introducing a British Bill of Rights

## Defense and Foreign Policy
Security commitments include:

- Maintaining Armed Forces with army not below 82,000
- Retaining Trident nuclear deterrent
- Meeting NATO's 2% GDP defense spending target
- Honoring the Armed Forces Covenant
- Maintaining 0.7% of national income for international development

## Constitutional Reform
Devolution and democratic proposals:

- Implementing "English votes for English laws"
- Delivering Smith Commission recommendations for Scotland
- Implementing Welsh devolution settlement
- Supporting the Stormont House Agreement in Northern Ireland

## Pensioners
Retirement security measures:

- Maintaining the triple lock on State Pension
- Taking family homes out of Inheritance Tax for most couples (£1 million threshold)
- Protecting pensioner benefits (bus passes, TV licenses, Winter Fuel Payment)
- Capping residential care costs

The manifesto concludes by emphasizing Conservative values of rewarding hard work, enabling social mobility, and believing in Britain's potential for continued greatness.
